analysis:
The supplied units are base-side text excerpts (lines 4931-5336 and 5337-5433) of docs/architecture/inference.md. The PR changes only documentation: a date bump, a Gemma `ClusterTensorParallelChoice.fastest` placement note around head lines 3635-3638, and a new Gemma 4 tensor-parallel foundation section around head lines 4037-4240. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the new Gemma section was not visible in full. No executable code, configuration, keys, authorization or wire contracts change in the visible evidence.

The base text I reviewed covers Qwen27 TP media, native-context request charging, cluster media ingress, pair capability honesty, cluster runtime approval facts and TP assistant batching. These are baseline descriptions that the PR does not touch. They raise no new security regression relative to the threat model. Relevant existing boundaries are TB-007 (inference engine and prefix cache, T-041), TB-002 (coordinator-provider websocket) and TB-011 (authorization). The excerpts state that media ingress disables prefix reuse and that cleanup failure retains charges; I saw nothing contradicting T-041 or the SEC-035 accepted risk.

Unverified: the base excerpts are not the changed lines, so I could not confirm the content of the new Gemma tensor-parallel section (head 4037-4240). If that section describes new code paths for Gemma TP (sealed collectives, prefix partitions, memory admission), a later pass with the full patch should check them against T-041, T-028 and the TB-007 mitigations. This documentation-only evidence offers no concrete basis for a finding, and no threat-model gap is introduced by the visible changes.
